cards.b: Infectious disease has shaped history: the Black Death, smallpox, the 1918 flu and COVID-19. Public health, meaning clean water, vaccines and surveillance, has saved more lives than most drugs. This lesson ties microbes, immunity and society together.

Infectious: caused by germs and can spread (cholera, TB, malaria). Non-communicable: not spread, such as diabetes, heart disease and cancer. Deficiency and genetic diseases form other groups. Disease spreads through air, water, food, vectors (mosquitoes), blood or contact.

• Endemic: steady in a region (malaria in some districts).
  • Epidemic: sudden rise in a place.
  • Pandemic: spread across the world (1918 flu, COVID-19, declared March 2020).

R0 is how many people one case infects on average. Above 1, the outbreak grows; below 1, it fades. Control tools: vaccination, isolation, masks, clean water, vector control, contact tracing. John Snow (1854) traced cholera in London to the Broad Street pump, the start of epidemiology.

• Malaria: Plasmodium, spread by female Anopheles. Ronald Ross showed this in 1897 in India (Secunderabad).
  • TB: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, airborne.
  • HIV/AIDS: virus attacks helper T cells.
  • Dengue, chikungunya: Aedes mosquitoes.
  • Cholera, typhoid: contaminated water.

Many new diseases jump from animals: Ebola, SARS, MERS, COVID-19, Nipah, avian flu. Habitat loss and wildlife trade raise the chance. The 'One Health' idea links human, animal and environmental health.

Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, the first human disease wiped out. Polio is nearly gone. Rinderpest in cattle was eradicated in 2011. Wuchereria and Guinea worm are close to elimination. mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 were developed within a year (Karikó and Weissman, Nobel 2023).

Fix these

  • Pandemic means wide spread, not severity.
  • Not all disease is caused by germs.
  • Vaccines and hygiene, not just drugs, are the main tools.

The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme tackles malaria and dengue. The TB programme (now NTEP) offers free DOTS treatment. India eliminated Guinea worm (2000) and trachoma as a public health problem (2024), and was declared maternal and neonatal tetanus free in 2015. Ayushman Bharat (2018) provides health insurance, and the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (2004) tracks outbreaks. ICMR's National Institute of Virology in Pune isolated the first SARS-CoV-2 strain in India in 2020. Malaria deaths fell sharply since 2000.

• Infectious versus non-communicable diseases.
  • Endemic, epidemic, pandemic.
  • R below 1 ends an outbreak.
  • Zoonoses are a rising threat; One Health is the answer.

Think about it:

  1. Why did smallpox eradication succeed but measles has not yet?
  2. How would you decide when to close schools in an outbreak?
